title: agent-parser: replace the WASM SQLite driver with modernc.org/sqlite

description:
agent-parser reads OpenCode databases through `github.com/ncruces/go-sqlite3`, which runs SQLite as WASM. Replace it with `modernc.org/sqlite`, a pure Go driver. Do not use a cgo driver: devhost release artifacts are cross-compiled with `CGO_ENABLED=0` (`apps/devhost/scripts/buildReleaseArtifacts.ts`).

The driver is registered in one place, `opencode.go`, and used through `database/sql`. agent-watcher names the module in `go.mod` for its tests and inherits the runtime dependency through agent-parser, so its `go.mod` and test fixtures change too. devhost has no SQLite dependency today and gains this one when it adopts agent-watcher.

Checked with a throwaway probe of `modernc.org/sqlite` v1.61.0, built with `CGO_ENABLED=0`:
- The current DSN works unchanged: `mode=ro` rejected a write, and `_pragma` set `busy_timeout` to 5000 and `foreign_keys` on.
- The driver name changes from `sqlite3` to `sqlite`.
- It compiles for `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64` and `darwin/arm64`.

Still to check:
- `OpenOpencodeDB` also has a `file::memory:?cache=shared` DSN, which the probe did not cover.
- Reads must stay safe while OpenCode is writing to the database.
- Binary size will grow. A minimal program using this driver built to 10.0 MB, while the full agent-watcher scanner probe with the WASM driver built to 4.5 MB. Compare real builds, along with startup and query time.
- Update the `rust` counterpart only if it shares the dependency.

Done when agent-parser and agent-watcher pass their tests on the new driver, `go mod tidy` removes the WASM modules from both, and a `CGO_ENABLED=0` build reads a real OpenCode database.
